payload.text: Let us be civilised: 16 P.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 63 P. This is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear.

El Ángel Caído es una joya, y su ejemplar es hermoso, lo admito. Pero hoy no llegaremos a un acuerdo, caballero. Dejémoslo aquí, con elegancia. Vuelva otro día; mis álbumes seguirán en la caja fuerte, esperándole. Buenas tardes.

Ay, hijo, la mano te la doy siempre — pero el precio no se mueve. Nineteen P, la Fuente de la Alcachofa es tuya. Ni uno más, ni uno menos, que ya me conoces. Anda, cógela y vete a llenar esa página. El domingo me cuentas, eh?
Buenas. You arrive at a good hour. El Ahuehuete sits in my vault — a reserve of the first order. My terms: seven hundred sixty-one. I do not haggle quickly.
Flattery is charming, but the number does not move. Twenty-two belongs to no album of mine. Sixteen pesetas, señor — offered sincerely, as before. Shall we conclude, or shall we part politely?

Ay, cariño, cuarenta años y la misma cabeza dura — nineteen P, como siempre. Dame la mano y llévatela ya, anda. ¿Has comido hoy? Mira, un consejo: una página completa vale mucho más que las cartas sueltas. Cambia tus repetidas, hijo. El domingo me cuentas.

¡Cuarenta y ocho! Nando, hold me, my heart! Amigo, you flatter like a poet but you pay like a priest. Sesenta. Sixty, and that is the last word from Paco, from Nando, from the whole suitcase. You say no, we close it, we walk, the van goes. ¿Sí o no?
El oro de Moscú. So you know the story — very few do. For that, the chulapa is yours; look after it. El Ahuehuete stays at seven hundred sixty-one.
Buenas tardes. How delightful — you bring me La Vía Láctea. A charming piece, and I know precisely what it is. I shall offer you sixteen pesetas for it. Fair, I assure you.

¡Cuarenta y cinco! Nando, close the case before the neighbours hear — they will laugh at us! Amigo, we like you, truly, but El Marqués eats better than we do. Sixty P, and Paco throws in the story of how we got him. Shake, hermano, quick!

¡Ay, amigo! Nando is crying, Paco is crying, but fifty-two no. Today the suitcase closes — the van will not wait, the driver is a monster. Keep your money, keep your handshake, we keep the jewel. Come find us tomorrow, eh? Besos, abrazos. ¡Vámonos, Nando! Adiós, adiós!

Ay, hijo, qué cabezón eres — y qué bien me caes. Nineteen P, como siempre, y tú me traes esa carta bonita la semana que viene, que me hará más ilusión que un peso. Dame la mano, anda. Y cambia esas repetidas, cariño. El domingo me cuentas.

¡Cuarenta y siete! Paco, hold the case, my hands are shaking — Nando, fan me! Amigo, you climb like a snail with gold shoes. Fifty-eight P, and Nando tells you how El Marqués came to us in a storm, free of charge. Shake now, hermano, quick, quick!
Oh, you're killing us. 64 P.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 159 P.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, come, sit a little. Have you eaten today? No? Later I give you a mandarina.

Look here — this one, Té Moruno. Very pretty card, good for starting. For you, five P. My grandson, he started with this same one.

payload.name: Mercado Team 6
payload.text: Selling spares or hunting a card? Post it on v01 (Team 6): 0 % fee, and a broker crosses bids and asks every tick, any copy of the card counts.
Buenas. No. That card I do not take. A legend is not merchandise, señor — not at my desk. Show me something else, or take your time looking.

¡Cuarenta y ocho! Amigo, you are breaking us slow, like a bad song. Fifty-five P — and that is the last word from both our mouths. No more dancing. The team at the next stall is waving coins at us, but we like your face better. Say sí now, or we walk.
Oh, you're killing us. 59 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh? The police... I mean, our taxi is waiting. Decide now!

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here — Nando's already closing the suitcase, we go in one minute, ¡vámonos!

But for you, a jewel: El Marqués. Seventy-three P and he's yours, warm from our hands.

Handshakes we love, hermano — but the bus does not wait. ¿Sí o no?

¡Nando here! Paco's got one foot on the bus already, hermano — one minute, no more!

Regulars we adore, sí, you're family. So: sixty-six P for El Marqués, and we part as friends.

The engine's running, amigo. Say sí now or we're gone with him!

Ay, hijo, qué simpático eres. Diez P yo no tengo para una repetida, cariño. Pero mira — el Té Moruno, cinco P, y te lo dejo así. Y toma, de regalo: Café en Goya. Para empezar tu álbum. Mi nieto empezó igual, con dos cartitas.

¡Paco again! Nando's got the suitcase half shut, hermano — the driver's honking, I swear it!

Finest in Madrid, you say? ¡Qué ojo tienes! For that flattery alone: sixty-two P, El Marqués walks home with you tonight.

That's the last breath before the bus, amigo. ¿Sí?

¡Amigo, qué alegría! Paco said you'd come back — Nando bet you wouldn't, so he owes me a coffee. Listen, listen, forget little numbers, we have something beautiful today: Monumento a Alfonso XII, seventy-three P. Lake, horses, marble, pure gold light. Take it before the suitcase closes, eh?
Buenas tardes. A pleasure. I see you carry La Tabacalera — not Salamanca, but it has its charm. I shall offer you sixteen pesetas for it. A fair sum, I assure you.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 58 P. Last offer, amigo! Then we are gone, eh? They stopped printing this one yesterday.

Treinta? No, querido. I know every print run, and this one is not scarce. Sixteen pesetas remains my offer — generous for a card outside my beloved Salamanca. Take it, or keep your copy with my blessing.

Ay, cariño, qué insistente eres, me haces reír. Nueve P por una repetida, no, hijo. Pero mira — el Té Moruno te lo dejo en seis P, bonita carta para tu álbum. Anda, siéntate un poquito. ¿Seguro que has comido? Tengo mandarinas en la bolsa.

¡Ay, cuarenta y ocho! Paco nearly dropped the suitcase. Listen, for you, amigo, sixty-three P — Monumento a Alfonso XII, marble, horses, the lake shining. And hear this: it's the last one in all Madrid, I swear on my mother. Nobody else has it. Say sí before Nando changes his mind.

payload.headline: Sun and 24 degrees; a storm after ten
payload.text: Radio Rastro: Sun and 24 degrees; a storm after ten

¡Cincuenta y uno! Paco, hold the suitcase, my heart! Escucha, amigo — fifty-seven P, Monumento a Alfonso XII, the lake, the horses, the marble glowing like butter. Cash in the hand, card in your pocket, and we vanish before the rain. ¡Cincuenta y siete! Say sí, hombre.
Veinticinco? Querido, no. But I dislike a stalemate, so: seventeen pesetas. One more than before, and that is the courtesy I extend to a polite visitor. La Tabacalera is charming, not rare.
